pr_title: Fix duplicate template handling in Persistent Notifications
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Fixes an issue with the persistent notification services. The service
schema handled each value as a template, however, this is already handled
by the services from config. Nevertheless, it is used directly in code as well.

This PR adjusts the service schema to only render templates, else expect a string.
In the create method we now check if we are dealing with a template, before we
render it.

As an added bonus, this reduces the amount of useless Template renders (for non-templates).

issue_context.title: MQTT trigger.payload being interpreted as a dict when passed JSON
issue_context.body:
**The problem**

1. I create an automation with a MQTT trigger, and an action of persistent notification create, that includes a template of `message: '{{ trigger.payload }}'`
2. Submit a JSON payload to that topic
3. Get error in logs of "Error while executing automation automation.testing: template value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['message']"

It seems that the JSON payload is being parsed into a dict, and the dict being passed to the `message:`

Even using `message: '{{ trigger.payload | string }}'` still results in above error.

Expectation would be a persistent notification created with the string value of the MQTT message (ie, the string representation of the JSON)

**What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?**

core-2021.2.3

**What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?**

_No response_

**What type of installation are you running?**

Home Assistant OS

**Integration causing the issue**

MQTT, Persistent Notification

**Link to integration documentation on our website**

_No response_

**Example YAML snippet**

```yaml
alias: New Automation
description: ''
trigger:
  - platform: mqtt
    topic: z2m/family_room_scene_controller/91/0/scene/003
condition: []
action:
  - service: persistent_notification.create
    data:
      message: '{{ trigger.payload }}'
mode: single


```

**Example MQTT Payload**

```json
{ "time": 123412341234, "value": "Test" }

```



**Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?**

```txt
2021-02-28 18:35:16 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.automation.new_automation_2] New Automation: Error executing script. Invalid data for call_service at pos 1: template value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['message']
2021-02-28 18:35:16 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.automation.new_automation_2] Error while executing automation automation.new_automation_2: template value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['message']

```
comments: I was working with @emontnemery on Discord regarding this.

The reason why it fails is that the output of template `'{{ trigger.payload }}'` is a dict even though trigger.payload is a string.
It fails in the same way even if the template is changed to `'{{ trigger.payload | string }}'`
This seems like unwanted behavior.

> This seems like unwanted behavior.

This is actually correct behavior, however, the service schema for the persistent notification schema has not been adjusted correctly to handle these new types.

I'll open up a PR to adjust it.

Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`persistent_notification`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L352) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

review_comments:
I'm surprised this fixes it. 

When a template is static, we already don't render it but just return it from `async_render` (or parse it to create a new object if parse_result=True). 

Oh ha: this works because `cv.string` will extract the raw value again and so it's back to the old value.
